correctness.rationale: For finite connected graphs with strictly positive real edge hopping and local Markovian dephasing, the Hilbert-Schmidt dissipativity identity is exact: the real form is the negative sum of absorber row/column norms and dephaser commutator norms. A peripheral eigenoperator X must kill each trap cyclic subspace and commute with every dephaser projector. Writing X|s>=x_s|s> and choosing a trap f at graph distance d, the positive shortest-path sum <s|H^d|f> forces x_s=0. The commutator equation then extends annihilation to the H-Krylov spans of F∪S. The orthogonal complement D reduces H and gives unitary persistent matrix evolution; HS contraction rules out peripheral Jordan blocks. Thus survival converges to tr(P_D rho), exactly the coherent F∪S-sink value. On C_n, sink 0 and dephaser s, sine modes with n|2ks yield dim D=floor((g-1)/2), g=gcd(n,2s), and the stated initial-site survival g/(2n) if g does not divide 2a, otherwise zero. The root-of-unity identity includes g=1,2 and even-cycle antipodal endpoints.
risks: Proof requires strictly positive real edge hopping, connected graph, positive absorber rates and fixed-rate t→∞ before any rate-zero limit; magnetic edge phases could cancel shortest paths.

evidence: Local Markovian dephasing on a graph is a natural controllable physical perturbation; the all-graph formula and single-site ring threshold are exact, rather than a tiny numerical improvement.
value.rationale: Sparse positive local noise behaves as an exact asymptotic spectral filter determined solely by its support; this turns a difficult dissipative transport survival calculation into a finite Hamiltonian Krylov computation and separates where dephasing acts from how strongly it acts. Nontrivial dark states persist for special supports, and the explicit ring gcd law characterizes that arithmetic obstruction.
risks: No prediction for finite-time hitting or mean absorption time, and not valid for sign-changing/magnetic edge weights without shortest-path positivity.
